There is a solution to this problem, and it isn't legislative. Like it or not we're using the internet wrong! The TCP/IP stack was never meant to be secured. HTTP was never meant to be anything but stateless text linking and markup. Everything that has been done to extend the usefulness of the internet has been done as a bolt-on to protocols that were never meant to be used this way.

An analogy: If you're house is made of balsa wood, you can install a bank vault door as your front door and titanium bars across all your windows. The wall of your house is still insecure.

The answer? Protocol stack rewrite from the ground up. Everything is not only encrypted, but paired key, e.g. PGP, encrypted. HTTP is written to include the ability for an encrypted state. All this won't stop exploiting poorly written applications, but it will go a huge long way toward improving real security.

BTW: there was a push for this in the late 1990's. The FBI led the charge to kill the idea.
